title: multi-route-quota-overshoot-and-misattribution-on-concurrent-requests
creator: Aditi Rao
description: Summary: Several customers report observed token/credit consumption higher than expected when a single API key simultaneously issues requests that touch multiple routes (e.g., embeddings + chat) and during brief routing failovers. We see two distinct problems: 1) per-org and per-key counters sometimes double-count the same logical request when the request is split into sub-requests across routes; 2) quota attribution occasionally records consumption against the wrong route leading to confusing billing and quota exhaustion for the route owner. This ticket captures investigation, repro, proposed fixes, and rollout plan.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create an org with both per-org quota and per-route quotas; enable route-level metering (chat, embeddings).

2) Use a single API key bound to that org. From a single client, issue 200 concurrent multiplexed requests that trigger the runtime to fan-out: one sub-request to chat route, one to embeddings route. Set small token usage so counts are visible in dashboards.

3) Observe metrics: per-key ledger increments, per-route counters, and org aggregate in Console -> Billing -> Usage. Repeat with retries enabled (exponential backoff) and during controlled canary failover of routing policy to secondary model variant.

4) Expected: aggregate usage equals sum of logical requests; each route shows only its own tokens. Observed: aggregate > logical (double-counting) and route A shows consumption that should be attributed to route B intermittently.
investigation_notes: Initial triage (2026-02-20): correlated spikes with routing changes and high concurrency. Dashboards show per-route 'ingest' counters incremented twice for the same request id in ~4.7% of sampled traces.

Trace analysis (2026-02-23): discovered repeated ledger writes where the rate-limiter lookup returned a stale policy object due to caching TTL + concurrent cache invalidation during canary rollout. Two worker threads processed the same logical request: one applied per-route decrement, the other applied per-org decrement, but both also applied per-key decrement because dedup key absent across the fan-out boundary.

Root cause hypothesis (2026-02-25): combination of (A) non-atomic multi-decrement across routes, (B) missing request-level idempotency key when a request is split into child requests, and (C) cache invalidation race that caused policy resolution to flip mid-flight, leading to duplicate accounting paths.
Additional note: retries and failovers exacerbate the issue because retry logic issues new sub-requests without propagating the parent idempotency key.
decision: Implement a two-part fix: 1) enforce propagation of a request-scope idempotency token across fan-out sub-requests so ledger writes are deduplicated; 2) change rate-limiter to perform a single coordinated atomic decrement for multi-route fanouts at the policy-router layer rather than independent decrements per sub-request. Short-term mitigation: increase cache TTL and block concurrent cache invalidation events during rollouts for affected routes.
implementation_plan: 1) Add 'x-rw-request-id' header propagation in runtime fan-out code path (PR DRAFT: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8421).
2) Extend ledger API to accept a list of route targets and perform an atomic debit on behalf of the parent request (backend change: billing-service#issue-204).
3) Add server-side dedup index keyed by (request-id, api-key) with short TTL to avoid double decrements when duplicates arrive within 5s.
4) Update retry library to forward request-id and to treat 409/429 as potentially idempotent with the idempotency header present.
5) Add unit/integration tests that simulate concurrent fan-out and cache invalidation during canary transitions.
6) Coordinate with Console team to add a temporary alert for per-key vs org aggregate divergence (>5% for 5m).
Estimated work split: backend 5d, runtime fan-out changes 3d, tests and rollout 2d.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): deploy ledger dedupe and request-id propagation to canary region (eu-west-1) with 5% traffic for 48 hours. Monitor divergence alert and per-route attribution metrics.
Phase 2 (gradual): increase to 25% for 24h, then 50% for 12h. If no regressions, push global and enable atomic multi-debit path.
Phase 3 (cleanup): after safe rollout, lower dedupe TTL to 2s and remove temporary cache TTL bump. Backfill missing metrics for affected window if needed.
Rollback criteria: any sustained increase in 5xxs > 0.5% or increase in median latency of billing calls > 200ms or customer complaints of unexpected charge increases tied to new ledger behavior.
qa_criteria: Automated tests covering: concurrent fan-out with same request-id -> single ledger decrement.
Integration test: simulate canary-induced cache invalidation while 200 concurrent requests are in-flight; assert no double-counting in the ledger and stable per-route attribution.
Manual verification steps: run repro harness and confirm Console usage shows expected aggregates; validate one affected customer's account in staging mirrors production fix.
Load test: benchmark billing latency under typical 2000 RPS production mix; ensure <10ms added p99 latency for ledger calls.
notes: Follow up with PM (Evelyn Chen) for customer communication templates and potential pro-rating credits for impacted customers.
Design input required for Console change to surface per-request idempotency link in usage detail (DES-4123).
Keep legal and compliance on CC for any retroactive billing adjustments.
